questions.question: The word "biology" is derived from which Greek words?
questions.explanation: Biology is derived from the Greek words "bios" meaning "life" and "logos" meaning "study."

questions.question: What does "bios" mean in Greek?
questions.explanation: "Bios" is the Greek word for "life."

questions.question: What does "logos" mean in Greek?
questions.explanation: "Logos" is the Greek word for "study."

questions.question: Biology is defined as the study of all of the following EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Biology is the study of living organisms, their origins, anatomy, morphology, physiology, behaviour, and distribution. Rocks are studied in geology.

questions.question: Which branch of biology deals with the study of organisms' structures?
questions.explanation: Anatomy is the study of organisms' structures.

questions.question: Which branch of biology studies the chemical reactions required for life to exist and function?
questions.explanation: Biochemistry is the study of the chemical reactions required for life to exist and function, usually a focus on the cellular level.

questions.question: Which branch of biology involves the use of information technology for the study, collection, and storage of genomic and other biological data?
questions.explanation: Bioinformatics is the use of information technology for the study, collection, and storage of genomic and other biological data.

questions.question: Which branch of biology deals with the manipulation of living matter, including genetic modification and synthetic biology?
questions.explanation: Biotechnology is the study of the manipulation of living matter, including genetic modification and synthetic biology.

questions.question: Which branch of biology is concerned with the study of plants?
questions.explanation: Botany is the study of plants.

questions.question: Which branch of biology studies the cell as a complete unit?
questions.explanation: Cell biology is the study of the cell as a complete unit, and the molecular and chemical interactions that occur within a living cell.

questions.question: Which branch of biology deals with the interactions of living organisms with one another and with the non-living elements of their environment?
questions.explanation: Ecology is the study of the interactions of living organisms with one another and with the non-living elements of their environment.

questions.question: Which branch of biology is the study of genes and heredity?
questions.explanation: Genetics is the study of genes and heredity.

questions.question: Which branch of biology deals with the study of the immune system?
questions.explanation: Immunology is the study of the immune system.

questions.question: Which branch of biology studies microscopic organisms and their interactions with other living things?
questions.explanation: Microbiology is the study of microscopic organisms (microorganisms) and their interactions with other living things.

questions.question: Which branch of biology studies biology and biological functions at the molecular level?
questions.explanation: Molecular biology is the study of biology and biological functions at the molecular level, some cross over with biochemistry.

questions.question: Which branch of biology deals with the study of diseases and their causes, processes, nature, and development?
questions.explanation: Pathobiology or pathology is the study of diseases, and the causes, processes, nature, and development of disease.

questions.question: Which branch of biology studies the interactions between drugs and organisms?
questions.explanation: Pharmacology is the study of the interactions between drugs and organisms.

questions.question: Which branch of biology studies the functions and mechanisms occurring in living organisms?
questions.explanation: Physiology is the study of the functions and mechanisms occurring in living organisms.

questions.question: Which branch of biology is the study of animals, including classification, physiology, development, and behaviour?
questions.explanation: Zoology is the study of animals, including classification, physiology, development, and behaviour.

questions.question: The term "living things" refers to any organism that possesses:
questions.explanation: Living things refers to any organism or a living form that possesses the characteristics of life or being alive.

questions.question: Living things include all of the following EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Living things include plants, animals, and microorganisms. Rocks are non-living.

questions.question: Living things were initially classified as:
questions.explanation: Living things were initially classified as a plant or an animal.

questions.question: Both plants and animals are:
questions.explanation: Both plants and animals are eukaryotic.

questions.question: Animals are basically living organisms that are:
questions.explanation: Animals are basically living organisms that are motile and heterotrophic.

questions.question: Plants are living organisms that are:
questions.explanation: Plants are non-motile, photosynthetic, and have a cell wall.

questions.question: Why are bacteria neither plants nor animals?
questions.explanation: Bacteria are neither plants nor animals mainly because they are prokaryotes.

questions.question: Which of the following contain only single-celled organisms?
questions.explanation: The bacteria and archaea contain only single-celled organisms.

questions.question: Both archaea and bacteria have cell walls, but:
options: Their cell walls are of different materials
Their cell membrane covers the cell wall
questions.explanation: Both archaea and bacteria have cell walls, but their cell walls are made up of different materials.

questions.question: Archaea and bacteria lack:
questions.explanation: Archaea and bacteria lack a nucleus.

questions.question: The classification of living things includes how many levels?
questions.explanation: The classification of living things includes 7 levels.

questions.question: The correct order of classification levels from largest to smallest is:
options: Kingdom, phylum, classes, order, families, genes, species
Kingdom, phylum, order, classes, families, genes, species
Species, genes, families, order, classes, phylum, kingdom
Phylum, kingdom, classes, order, families, genes, species
questions.explanation: The classification of living things includes 7 levels namely: kingdom, phylum, classes, order, families, genes, and species.

questions.question: The most fundamental classification of living things is:
questions.explanation: The most fundamental classification of living things is kingdoms.

questions.question: How many kingdoms are there currently?
questions.explanation: There are five kingdoms currently (Animalia, Plantae, Monera, Protista, Fungi).

questions.question: The five kingdoms are:
questions.explanation: The five kingdoms are Animalia, Plantae, Monera, Protista, and Fungi.

questions.question: Living things are placed into kingdoms based on all of the following EXCEPT:
options: Types of cells they make in the body
The number of cells they contain
questions.explanation: Living things are placed into kingdoms based on how they acquire their food, types of cells they make in the body, and the number of cells they contain.

questions.question: Which level comes immediately after kingdom in classification?
questions.explanation: The phylum is the next level in the classification of living things followed by the kingdom.

questions.question: Phylum is an attempt to find some kind of physical resemblance among organisms within a kingdom, suggesting:
options: They live in the same habitat
questions.explanation: Physical similarities suggest that there is a common ancestry among the organisms in a particular phylum.

questions.question: Classes are the way to further subdivide organisms of a:
questions.explanation: Classes are the way to further subdivide organisms of a phylum.

questions.question: Humans belong to which class because they drink milk as a baby?
questions.explanation: Humans belong to the mammal class because they drink milk as a baby.

questions.question: What is used to determine to which order an organism belongs?
questions.explanation: A taxonomy key is used to determine to which the organism belongs to.

questions.question: A taxonomy key is:
options: A checklist of characteristics that determine how organisms are grouped together
A list of all known species
questions.explanation: A taxonomy key is nothing but a checklist of the characteristics that determine how the organisms are grouped together.

questions.question: Orders are divided into:
questions.explanation: Orders are divided into families.

questions.question: Organisms within a family have more in common than with organisms in any classification level above it. Because of familiarity, the organisms of a family are said to be:
questions.explanation: Because of familiarity, the organisms of a family are said to be related to each other.

questions.question: Genus is a way to characterize the:
questions.explanation: Genus is a way to characterize the generic name for an organism.

questions.question: When using taxonomy to name an organism, the genus is used to complete:
options: The second part of its two-part name
The first part of its two-part name
questions.explanation: When using taxonomy to name an organism, the genus is used to complete the first part of its two-part name.

questions.question: What is the lowest and most exacting level of classification of living things?
questions.explanation: Species are as specific as you can get. It is the lowest and most exacting level of classification of living things.

questions.question: The main pattern for an organism to be placed in a particular species is:
options: The ability to breed with other organisms
Mode of nutrition of the organisms
questions.explanation: The main pattern for an organism to be placed in a particular species is the ability to breed with other organisms of that same species.

questions.question: The species of an organism regulates:
options: The first part of its two-part name
The second part of its two-part name
questions.explanation: The species of an organism regulates the second part of its two-part name.

questions.question: Which kingdom has prokaryotic cells, a non-cellulosic cell wall, and no nuclear membrane?
questions.explanation: Monera has prokaryotic cells, a non-cellulosic cell wall, and no nuclear membrane.

questions.question: Which kingdom is unicellular with a cell wall and autotrophic nutrition?
questions.explanation: Protista is unicellular with a cell wall and autotrophic nutrition.
